content.thinking:
The latest output from the salvage run indicates a CUDA OOM error. The tail of `/tmp/salvage.log` shows a stack trace ending with `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.00 GiB... GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.35 GiB of which 2.58 GiB is free. Process 1367330 has 23.29 GiB memory in use.` This tells me that the salvage script has already launched a new Python process (pid 1367330) which is now hogging most of the GPU memory and failing during the flex_attention operation.

My goal is to get the salvage pipeline to complete successfully so I can collect the final results and later update `scores.md`. To do that I need to free GPU memory and restart the salvage script. The simplest way is to kill the offending process (pid 1367330) and then relaunch the salvage script (`/tmp/salvage_run.py`) the same way I did before, ensuring the repo root is on `sys.path` (that was already patched). 

Before killing, I want to verify the process is indeed the one I need to stop. I can use `ps -o pid,cmd -p 1367330` to print its command line. Then I’ll send a SIGKILL with `kill -9 1367330`. A short sleep ensures the OS cleans up. 

After killing, I should check if any other stray processes (like the Paperclip agent) are still running that might be contending for GPU memory. `pgrep -f "paperclip"` will list any such processes; I’ll just show the first few. Then I’ll query `nvidia-smi` for current GPU memory usage by remaining compute apps to confirm that memory is now free.

Finally, I’ll relaunch the salvage script in the background exactly as before: `nohup .venv/bin/python -u /tmp/salvage_run.py > /tmp/salvage.log 2>&1 & echo "pid $!"`. This will start a fresh run with a clean GPU state. 

All these steps fit into a single Bash command, separated by newlines, and I’ll wrap them in a tool call so the system executes them. This should resolve the OOM issue and allow the salvage pipeline to proceed to completion, after which I can collect the results and continue with the reporting tasks.

arguments.command:
ps -o pid,cmd -p 1367330 | tail -1; kill -9 1367330 2>/dev/null; sleep 2
pgrep -f "paperclip" | head; nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv,noheader
nohup .venv/bin/python -u /tmp/salvage_run.py > /tmp/salvage.log 2>&1 & echo "pid $!"
